references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew: One of those who were with Jesus drew his sword and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his ear ([ref:Matt 26:51|Matthew 26:51]).
Parallel passage in Mark: One of those standing there drew his sword and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his ear ([ref:Mark 14:47|Mark 14:47]).
John identifies the one who struck with the sword as Simon Peter, and the servant as Malchus. Peter cut off his right ear ([ref:Joh 18:10|John 18:10]).
Shortly before this event, Jesus had asked the disciples to buy swords, and they showed him two swords ([ref:Luk 22:36-38|Luke 22:36-38]). One of them was used here.
Immediately after this, Jesus stopped the disciples and healed the servant's ear—an event mentioned only in Luke ([ref:Luk 22:51|Luke 22:51]).

Jesus rebukes the one who used the sword and says that all who draw the sword will perish by the sword, and that he could have asked the Father for twelve legions of angels ([ref:Matt 26:52-54|Matthew 26:52-54]).
Jesus commands Peter to put his sword back in its sheath and asks if he should not drink the cup the Father has given him ([ref:Joh 18:11|John 18:11]).
